meet.headline: Titan And Echo Will Take It From Here
said:
Titan And Echo
Will Take It From Here
Echo, from here on we handle the updates. What is happening around the county, what the numbers actually did, and the bits of a house nobody thinks about until they leak.
And when I don't follow something, I'll say so. If it takes me two goes, it probably takes someone else two goes.

heat.headline: Check The Heat Before You Need It
said:
Check The Heat
Before You Need It
Echo, the NFPA counted 37,365 home heating fires a year from 2020 to 2024. Space heaters and heating stoves caused 30% of those fires — and 73% of the deaths.
Chimneys and heating systems get inspected and cleaned each year before the season — a licensed contractor's job
Anything that burns stays three feet clear of a heater — the spacing a fire department repeats every winter
A furnace that sat unused all summer is worth a look from a licensed HVAC contractor before the first cold night
Thirty percent of the fires. Seventy-three percent of the deaths. That gap stays with me.
heat.source: NFPA · Home Heating Fires, 2020–2024 annual averages · retrieved September 24, 2026

taxdate.headline: The Only Tax Due Date That Counts Is On Your Bill
said:
The Only Tax Due Date
That Counts Is On Your Bill
Echo, Georgia's default property tax due date is December 20. But a county can move it to December 1 or November 15, or split it into instalments.
So there's no single date for everybody. How do I find mine?
From the bill itself. Henry's office publishes no fixed date online — it says payment must reach them by the current due date, or carry a USPS postmark by it.
So the envelope is the instruction, not the calendar. I'd read the date on mine before I assumed December.
taxdate.source: Georgia Dept. of Revenue & Henry County Tax Commissioner · retrieved Sept 24, 2026

attorney.headline: In Georgia, An Attorney Closes Your Home Sale
said:
In Georgia, An Attorney
Closes Your Home Sale
Echo, in Georgia only a licensed Georgia attorney can close a home sale. The Georgia Supreme Court confirmed it in 2003.
Not my agent? I thought my agent took care of the whole thing.
Your agent guides the sale. The attorney handles the legal side of the closing, including the deed. Two different jobs.
So the agent guides it and the attorney closes it. Two jobs. I'd want that clear before closing day.
attorney.source: In re UPL Advisory Opinion 2003-2, 277 Ga. 472 (2003) · retrieved Oct 2, 2026

charging.headline: Know Where You Charge Your Phone And Tools
said:
Know Where You Charge
Your Phone And Tools
Echo, it's Fire Prevention Week. NFPA says lithium-ion batteries store a lot of energy in a small place and can overheat, start a fire, or explode if overcharged or damaged.
NFPA says to use the cable that came with the device. A licensed electrician can look at a worn outlet.
Charging goes on a hard surface, never under a pillow or on a bed or couch. Ask your fire department.
E-bikes, e-scooters and power tools charge best outside, away from doors and windows. A licensed contractor can advise.
A device that runs hot, smells strange, pops or changes shape: stop using it and call 9-1-1, the fire department.
A phone charger. I never thought of it as a fire question.
charging.source: NFPA · Fire Prevention Week lithium-ion battery lesson plan · retrieved Oct 2, 2026

loanestimate.headline: Ask More Than One Lender For A Loan Estimate
said:
Ask More Than One Lender
For A Loan Estimate
Echo, a Loan Estimate tells you the details of a mortgage loan you have asked for. The CFPB says to request more than one.
More than one? Isn't a loan just a loan?
The CFPB says the best way to tell if you have a competitive offer is to compare it with Loan Estimates from other lenders.
So I ask a few lenders before I choose one. That's how I'd know mine is a good one.
loanestimate.source: CFPB, Loan Estimate, consumerfinance.gov · retrieved Oct 9, 2026

closingdisclosure.headline: Your Closing Disclosure Should Come Early
said:
Your Closing Disclosure
Should Come Early
Echo, the CFPB says lenders are required to provide your Closing Disclosure three business days before your scheduled closing.
Three days. What am I supposed to do with them?
The CFPB says to use those days wisely, because now is the time to resolve problems. If something looks different than you thought, ask why.
So I read it early and ask about anything that looks off. That's what the days are for.
closingdisclosure.source: CFPB, Closing Disclosure, consumerfinance.gov · retrieved Oct 9, 2026

afterstorm.headline: Walk The Outside First Before You Go Back In
said:
Walk The Outside First
Before You Go Back In
Echo, after a big storm FEMA says to walk around the outside first and check for loose power lines, gas leaks and structural damage.
Treat any downed line as live and stay away. Report it to the power company. A licensed electrician checks the rest.
Do not wade through standing water; lines can charge it. A licensed contractor handles cleanup.
If you smell gas or hear hissing, leave and call the fire department. Use a flashlight, not a match.
If the building looks unstable, a qualified inspector or engineer should look before anyone goes in.
Outside first, then inside. I never thought to check the lines before the door.
afterstorm.source: FEMA and Ready.gov, returning home after a disaster · retrieved Oct 9, 2026

pumpkins.headline: Before The Pumpkins Go Out On The Porch
said:
Before The Pumpkins
Go Out On The Porch
Echo, NFPA says dried flowers, cornstalks and crepe paper catch fire easily. They belong away from open flames and heat like light bulbs and heaters.
NFPA points to a battery candle or a glow stick inside a jack-o-lantern. Your fire department can say more.
Lit pumpkins sit away from anything that burns and clear of doorsteps and walkways. Ask your fire department.
Exits stay clear of decorations, so nothing blocks the way out. Your fire department can talk it through.
Every smoke alarm in the home working before the 31st. A licensed electrician can check hardwired ones.
Cornstalks catch fire easily? …Oh. My whole porch is cornstalks. I'd move them away from the pumpkin first.
pumpkins.source: NFPA, Halloween Fire Safety Tips tip sheet · retrieved Oct 17, 2026

supply.headline: Buying In South Metro What Months Of Supply Means
said:
Buying In South Metro
What Months Of Supply Means
Echo, months of supply is how long it would take to sell every home for sale at today's pace. Henry County was at 6.8 months in September.
Is that a lot?
A year earlier it was 5.3. Clayton, Newton, Fayette and Spalding were also higher than last year. Rockdale was about the same.
More months of supply? …Oh. That means more homes out there. I'd look at a few before I pick one.
supply.source: Multiple Listing Service via Simply List Atlanta · September 2026 · read October 23, 2026

More homes. Are fewer of them selling?
No. 159 homes sold in Henry in September, about the same as the 160 a year ago. Four other counties had more homes for sale too.
More homes, about the same sales? …Oh. I was going to list high and wait. I'd rethink that.
competition.source: Multiple Listing Service via Simply List Atlanta · September 2026 · read October 23, 2026

alarms.headline: When The Clocks Go Back Check Your Smoke Alarms
said:
When The Clocks Go Back
Check Your Smoke Alarms
Echo, clocks go back one hour on Sunday, November 1. The U.S. Fire Administration has a few simple steps for smoke alarms.
Smoke alarms get tested monthly, says the U.S. Fire Administration. Your fire department can say more.
Batteries yearly, the whole alarm every 10 years, per the U.S. Fire Administration. Ask your fire department.
Alarms go inside and outside each bedroom and on every level. A licensed electrician can check hardwired ones.
Once a month? …Oh. I only check mine when the clocks change. I'd start this weekend.
alarms.source: U.S. Fire Administration, Smoke Alarms · Fox 29, clock change date · read October 23, 2026

builder.headline: Rockdale Now Allows Smaller Homes On Eligible Lots
said:
Rockdale Now Allows
Smaller Homes On Eligible Lots
Echo, Rockdale County's new development code took effect October 1. Owners on eligible lots can add a smaller second home.
A second home on the same lot? What does that open up?
Think guest cottage or in-law suite on the same lot as the main house. The code also sets standards for tiny home and cottage home villages.
So a parent could move in next door, and a buyer gets one more kind of home to look at. I only need a lot first.
builder.source: Rockdale County news release · rockdalecountyga.gov · posted October 26, 2026

pricecuts.headline: Selling In South Metro Atlanta Listings Down 26.5%
said:
Selling In South Metro
Atlanta Listings Down 26.5%
Echo, fewer homes are coming up for sale in metro Atlanta. New listings were down 26.5% from a year ago, over the four weeks ending Oct 25.
So what does that mean for a seller?
A seller has fewer new homes competing for buyers. Homes going under contract fell 25.9%, so fewer buyers are signing on too.
So fewer new homes to pick from and fewer buyers signing. I can barely pick a lunch spot.
pricecuts.source: Redfin weekly housing report · four weeks ending Oct 25, 2026 · released Oct 29, 2026

faucets.headline: Fallen Leaves Make Free Mulch Mow Them, Don't Bag Them
said: H4

Fallen Leaves Make Free Mulch
Mow Them, Don't Bag Them
Echo, if you don't want to rake, just run the mower over the leaves. Set it on its highest setting, and chopped leaves are useful around the yard.
Mulch: use chopped leaves in garden beds and around young plants.
In the cold they help protect young or tender plants.
Compost: chopped leaves are a good addition to a compost pile.
Soil: as they break down, chopped leaves add organic matter to the soil.
Mulch, compost and richer soil. Those leaves work harder than I do.
faucets.source: Colorado State University Extension, Using Leaves in the Landscape, reviewed July 2024 · read Oct 30, 2026

Homes Took A Bit Longer
To Sell In September
Henry County · September 2026
Days On Market
68 last year
New Listings
388 in August
Echo, Realtor.com says the median home in Henry County sat on the market 63 days in September, up from 59 in August. New listings were 390.
Last September the median was 68 days
Counts single-family homes, condos and townhomes
Median? …Oh, the middle one. So a little slower than August, but quicker than last year.
entries.source: Realtor.com via FRED · Henry County, GA median days on market and new listings · retrieved Oct 9, 2026

entries.headline: Your Closing Disclosure Should Come Early
said:
Your Closing Disclosure
Should Come Early
Echo, the CFPB says lenders are required to provide your Closing Disclosure three business days before your scheduled closing.
Three days. What am I supposed to do with them?
The CFPB says to use those days wisely, because now is the time to resolve problems. If something looks different than you thought, ask why.
So I read it early and ask about anything that looks off. That's what the days are for.
entries.source: CFPB, Closing Disclosure, consumerfinance.gov · retrieved Oct 9, 2026

entries.headline: Walk The Outside First Before You Go Back In
said:
Walk The Outside First
Before You Go Back In
Echo, after a big storm FEMA says to walk around the outside first and check for loose power lines, gas leaks and structural damage.
Treat any downed line as live and stay away. Report it to the power company. A licensed electrician checks the rest.
Do not wade through standing water; lines can charge it. A licensed contractor handles cleanup.
If you smell gas or hear hissing, leave and call the fire department. Use a flashlight, not a match.
If the building looks unstable, a qualified inspector or engineer should look before anyone goes in.
Outside first, then inside. I never thought to check the lines before the door.
entries.source: FEMA and Ready.gov, returning home after a disaster · retrieved Oct 9, 2026

entries.headline: Buying In South Metro More Homes In Most Counties
said:
Buying In South Metro
More Homes In Most Counties
Echo, FMLS numbers for August show more homes for sale than a year earlier in Henry, Clayton, Fayette and Spalding counties.
All of South Metro? So buyers have more to pick from everywhere?
Not everywhere. Rockdale and Newton had slightly fewer. Henry, the biggest, had 1,016 homes for sale, up 14.5% from a year earlier.
Most counties, not all. …Oh. Where I look matters as much as when.
entries.source: FMLS via Simply List Atlanta, August 2026 county reports · retrieved Oct 17, 2026

entries.headline: Selling In South Metro Sold At 96% Of Asking
said:
Selling In South Metro
Sold At 96% Of Asking
Echo, FMLS numbers for August show Henry County homes sold for about 96% of their first asking price. That's up from a year ago.
96%? That's almost full price.
And that held even with 397 new listings in August, up 15.7%. Homes still sold 12.5% faster than last year.
More competition, same strong price. …Oh. So the first price is the one to get right.
entries.source: FMLS via Simply List Atlanta, Henry County report, August 2026 · retrieved Oct 17, 2026

entries.headline: Before The Pumpkins Go Out On The Porch
said:
Before The Pumpkins
Go Out On The Porch
Echo, NFPA says dried flowers, cornstalks and crepe paper catch fire easily. They belong away from open flames and heat like light bulbs and heaters.
NFPA points to a battery candle or a glow stick inside a jack-o-lantern. Your fire department can say more.
Lit pumpkins sit away from anything that burns and clear of doorsteps and walkways. Ask your fire department.
Exits stay clear of decorations, so nothing blocks the way out. Your fire department can talk it through.
Every smoke alarm in the home working before the 31st. A licensed electrician can check hardwired ones.
Cornstalks catch fire easily? …Oh. My whole porch is cornstalks. I'd move them away from the pumpkin first.
entries.source: NFPA, Halloween Fire Safety Tips tip sheet · retrieved Oct 17, 2026

entries.headline: Buying In South Metro What Months Of Supply Means
said:
Buying In South Metro
What Months Of Supply Means
Echo, months of supply is how long it would take to sell every home for sale at today's pace. Henry County was at 6.8 months in September.
Is that a lot?
A year earlier it was 5.3. Clayton, Newton, Fayette and Spalding were also higher than last year. Rockdale was about the same.
More months of supply? …Oh. That means more homes out there. I'd look at a few before I pick one.
entries.source: Multiple Listing Service via Simply List Atlanta · September 2026 · read October 23, 2026

More homes. Are fewer of them selling?
No. 159 homes sold in Henry in September, about the same as the 160 a year ago. Four other counties had more homes for sale too.
More homes, about the same sales? …Oh. I was going to list high and wait. I'd rethink that.

entries.headline: When The Clocks Go Back Check Your Smoke Alarms
said:
When The Clocks Go Back
Check Your Smoke Alarms
Echo, clocks go back one hour on Sunday, November 1. The U.S. Fire Administration has a few simple steps for smoke alarms.
Smoke alarms get tested monthly, says the U.S. Fire Administration. Your fire department can say more.
Batteries yearly, the whole alarm every 10 years, per the U.S. Fire Administration. Ask your fire department.
Alarms go inside and outside each bedroom and on every level. A licensed electrician can check hardwired ones.
Once a month? …Oh. I only check mine when the clocks change. I'd start this weekend.
entries.source: U.S. Fire Administration, Smoke Alarms · Fox 29, clock change date · read October 23, 2026

entries.headline: Rockdale Now Allows Smaller Homes On Eligible Lots
said:
Rockdale Now Allows
Smaller Homes On Eligible Lots
Echo, Rockdale County's new development code took effect October 1. Owners on eligible lots can add a smaller second home.
A second home on the same lot? What does that open up?
Think guest cottage or in-law suite on the same lot as the main house. The code also sets standards for tiny home and cottage home villages.
So a parent could move in next door, and a buyer gets one more kind of home to look at. I only need a lot first.
entries.source: Rockdale County news release · rockdalecountyga.gov · posted October 26, 2026

entries.headline: Selling In South Metro Atlanta Listings Down 26.5%
said:
Selling In South Metro
Atlanta Listings Down 26.5%
Echo, fewer homes are coming up for sale in metro Atlanta. New listings were down 26.5% from a year ago, over the four weeks ending Oct 25.
So what does that mean for a seller?
A seller has fewer new homes competing for buyers. Homes going under contract fell 25.9%, so fewer buyers are signing on too.
So fewer new homes to pick from and fewer buyers signing. I can barely pick a lunch spot.
entries.source: Redfin weekly housing report · four weeks ending Oct 25, 2026 · released Oct 29, 2026

entries.headline: Fallen Leaves Make Free Mulch Mow Them, Don't Bag Them
said: H4

Fallen Leaves Make Free Mulch
Mow Them, Don't Bag Them
Echo, if you don't want to rake, just run the mower over the leaves. Set it on its highest setting, and chopped leaves are useful around the yard.
Mulch: use chopped leaves in garden beds and around young plants.
In the cold they help protect young or tender plants.
Compost: chopped leaves are a good addition to a compost pile.
Soil: as they break down, chopped leaves add organic matter to the soil.
Mulch, compost and richer soil. Those leaves work harder than I do.
entries.source: Colorado State University Extension, Using Leaves in the Landscape, reviewed July 2024 · read Oct 30, 2026
